source.title: Kernel interpolation generalizes poorly
source.authors: Yicheng Li; Haobo Zhang; Qian Lin

record.tranche_reason: The paper discusses benign overfitting and cites double-descent work, but its own results bound generalization error for interpolants; it does not test any of the specified curve shapes or their proposed explanations.
record.gate_note: The paper reports theoretical generalization-error lower bounds for kernel interpolation and overfitted wide neural networks. These do not measure model-size, epoch, or sample-size curves, so they are recorded as findings about the claim's subject under versions ["none"]. Results cited from other work are not extracted.
record.test_reason: The paper proves lower bounds, about cσ²n^−ε, on the generalization error of kernel minimum-norm interpolants and of infinitely trained wide two-layer ReLU networks on the sphere, both in fixed dimension. It runs no sweep over model size, epochs or sample size and compares no risk before and after an interpolation threshold. Its result bears on benign overfitting, meaning whether interpolants can be near-optimal. It does not bear on the shape of a double-descent curve. A poor interpolant error rate is compatible with a second descent existing, so no version is tested.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct. Under mild conditions, kernel interpolation generalizes poorly, with error Ω(n^−ε) for any ε>0. As a corollary, overfitted wide networks on the sphere generalize poorly. The authors suggest benign overfitting needs explaining from another perspective. They note (Remark 3.2) that the theorem does not formally imply inconsistency.
record.recipe_differences: The study proves asymptotic lower bounds for interpolation under theoretical assumptions; it does not reproduce the original double-descent sweeps.
record.method_sensitivity: No outcome-changing sweep is reported; the results are stated under specified kernel, noise, data-distribution, initialization, and asymptotic conditions.

fits_no_version.finding: In fixed dimension with non-vanishing noise, kernel minimum-norm interpolation has a high-probability lower bound on L2 error of cσ²n^−ε for any ε>0. The bound covers Sobolev, periodic and dot-product kernels, including the NTK.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Benign overfitting fails for kernel interpolation in fixed dimension: interpolants cannot attain near-optimal rates.

fits_no_version.finding: Wide two-layer ReLU networks on the sphere, trained by gradient flow to t→∞ with symmetric initialization, inherit the same lower bound on limiting error.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Overfitted wide networks in the NTK regime on the sphere generalize poorly in fixed dimension.

record.problems: The results are asymptotic lower bounds rather than measured curve shapes. The authors note that Theorem 3.1 does not imply inconsistency. The neural-network result concerns the overparameterized, infinite-time regime on the sphere, not a sweep over widths or training times.
record.rows_left_out: No applicable results left out. Results cited from other studies, including prior double-descent and interpolation results, were not extracted.

untested.parts: No model-size sweep or test-error curve for deep networks.
No test error over training time.
No comparison of test error across sample sizes near an interpolation threshold.
No capacity sweep and no comparison of risk below and above the interpolation point. The kernel interpolant is analysed only at one end of the curve.
No effective-complexity measure is tested for predicting a peak location.
No peak analysis. The paper cites that KRR with a properly chosen λ is minimax optimal, but it does not test whether a peak disappears under tuned regularization.
No re-counting of complexity by effective parameters.

record.verdict_notes: The paper is purely theoretical, with no experiments. It is related to V4 and V6 only indirectly, through the benign-overfitting literature it cites (including Belkin et al. 2019, an original source). Its claims concern interpolant error rates, not curve shape, so no verdict labels are given. The reader's T6 and discusses classification is kept.

versions.untested_parts: No model-size sweep or test-error curve.
No test-error curve over training epochs.
No comparison across training sample sizes near an interpolation threshold.
No capacity sweep across model classes or comparison before and after interpolation.
No test of a shared effective-complexity measure across axes.
No peak analysis by noise or regularization, and no test for multiple peaks.
No re-counting of complexity by effective parameters or comparison of curve shapes.

rows.subject: kernel minimum-norm interpolant f_hat_inter
rows.operation_detail: Prove a high-probability lower bound on conditional expected L2 generalization error.

conditions.value: Assumptions 1–4: polynomial eigenvalue decay, embedding index, Hölder-continuous kernel, and non-vanishing conditional noise
n sufficiently large depending on ε and δ

rows.value: ≥ cσ² n^−ε for any ε > 0, with probability at least 1 − δ
rows.uncertainty: High-probability statement: at least 1 − δ; no error bar or confidence interval stated.
rows.note: The theorem gives a lower bound for interpolation error, not a comparison along a model-capacity axis or a double-descent curve.
rows.check: Link and state are correct. This is a theoretical lower bound for a single interpolating estimator, with no capacity, epoch or sample-size axis.

rows.subject: two-layer ReLU neural network f_hat_t^NN
rows.operation_detail: Derive a high-probability lower bound on the limiting generalization error of an overparameterized network.

conditions.value: Inputs uniformly distributed on the unit sphere S^(d−1)
Symmetric initialization as specified in Proposition 4.1
n and m sufficiently large depending on ε and δ

rows.value: ≥ cσ² n^−ε for any ε > 0, with probability at least 1 − δ over samples and initialization
rows.uncertainty: High-probability statement: at least 1 − δ; no error bar or confidence interval stated.
rows.note: This is a bound for the wide-network, infinite-training-time regime, not a test-error sweep over widths or epochs.
rows.check: Link and state are correct. This is a lower bound in the large-width, t→∞ regime. It is not a sweep over width or training time.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

relation.reason: The study discusses generalization after interpolation through benign overfitting, but neither tests double descent nor uses it as a tool.

tranche.reason: The asymptotic interpolation-error lower bounds do not establish or refute a double-descent curve, peak location, noise-dependent peak, or reparameterization of complexity.

source_check.notes: The results concern fixed dimension and non-vanishing conditional noise. Remark 3.2 explicitly states that the lower bound does not imply inconsistency; poor interpolation generalization alone does not rule out a second descent.
